package_info.why_malicious: Multiple cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in the FigCaption widget and widget handling allow attackers to inject arbitrary HTML, attributes, and classes into user-generated content. These flaws bypass expected sanitization, enabling stored and self-XSS, page defacement, and user redirection. The vulnerabilities break HTML sandboxing and can be exploited by low-privileged users to execute malicious scripts in the context of other users.

execution_context.trigger: During content creation or editing, and at runtime rendering of content
execution_context.file_location: CKEditor instance in Drupal content editor (client-side), content stored in Drupal database, rendered in page body
required_permissions: Ability to create or edit content (low-privileged user)
Potential network access if XSS payload is used for exfiltration

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: <figcaption class="cke_widget_editable" data-placeholder="Enter caption here" data-cke-widget-editable="caption" data-cke-enter-mode="2" data-cke-filter="46" data-cke-display-name="caption" contenteditable="true">I am a caption</figcaption>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During content creation or editing, the code allows arbitrary HTML and attributes to be inserted into the figcaption element, which is then stored in the Drupal database and rendered in the page body, resulting in the injection of malicious content or attributes into the DOM.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The snippet permits arbitrary HTML and attributes in a context that is rendered as part of the page, allowing attackers to inject malicious code or attributes that can alter page behavior or facilitate XSS.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict HTML and attributes in figcaption to a safe, predefined whitelist; here, arbitrary attributes and classes are allowed, breaking containment and enabling injection.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be to style captions or add semantic markup, but not to allow arbitrary classes or data attributes that could be abused for XSS or UI manipulation.
key_indicators: Lack of attribute sanitization in figcaption
Ability to inject arbitrary classes and data-* attributes
Presence of non-whitelisted attributes in rendered HTML

execution_context.trigger: During content creation or editing, and at runtime rendering of content
execution_context.file_location: CKEditor instance in Drupal content editor (client-side), content stored in Drupal database, rendered in page body
required_permissions: Ability to create or edit content

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During content creation or editing, the code injects an anchor tag with a global overlay class and an external link, which is stored in the Drupal database and rendered in the page body, causing the overlay to cover the UI and redirect user clicks to an attacker-controlled site.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The injected class (joyride-modal-bg) is typically used for overlays and, when combined with an external link, can hijack the UI and redirect users, enabling phishing or defacement.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal captions or content should not be able to overlay or hijack the entire UI or redirect users to external domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Overlay classes are used in legitimate modal dialogs, but not in user-generated captions or arbitrary content fields.
key_indicators: Use of global overlay class (joyride-modal-bg) in user content
Presence of external href to attacker-controlled domain
Overlay element covering the UI in rendered content

execution_context.trigger: During content creation or editing, and at runtime rendering of content
execution_context.file_location: CKEditor instance in Drupal content editor (client-side), content stored in Drupal database, rendered in page body
required_permissions: Ability to create or edit content
Potential network access if XSS payload is used for exfiltration

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During content creation or editing, the code injects an tag with a javascript: URL in the src attribute, which is stored in the Drupal database and rendered in the page body, potentially triggering JavaScript execution in the victim's browser if not properly sanitized.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of a javascript: URL in the src attribute is a classic XSS vector, allowing arbitrary script execution if not blocked by sanitization.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal sanitization should strip or block javascript: URLs in image src attributes to prevent script execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for javascript: URLs in image src attributes; images should reference valid image resources.
key_indicators: Presence of javascript: scheme in src or data-cke-saved-src attribute
Bypassing of URL scheme sanitization in image tags
Execution of JavaScript via image loading

execution_context.trigger: During content creation or editing, specifically in preview mode
execution_context.file_location: CKEditor instance in Drupal content editor (client-side, preview mode)
required_permissions: Ability to create or edit content

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During content creation or editing in preview mode, the code injects a <script> tag that is rendered and executed in the preview, resulting in arbitrary JavaScript execution (self-XSS) in the user's browser.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Direct injection and execution of <script> tags in preview mode allows attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript, demonstrating a clear XSS vulnerability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Preview mode should sanitize and block script tags to prevent execution of user-supplied JavaScript.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for script tags in user-generated content; script execution should always be blocked.
key_indicators: Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in preview mode
Lack of sanitization for <script> tags in content preview
Presence of <script> elements in user content

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts and submits malicious HTML payloads using FigCaption or widget attributes, such as arbitrary classes, javascript: URLs, or <script> tags, via the content editor.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is stored in the Drupal content database as part of user-generated content.

attack_chain.action: Stored payload is rendered in the CKEditor instance or on the public-facing page, causing the browser to process and execute the injected HTML, attributes, or scripts.
attack_chain.leads_to: XSS, page defacement, or user redirection occurs as the malicious content is executed in the victim's browser.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes in the victim's browser, enabling actions such as session hijacking, user redirection to attacker-controlled domains, or exfiltration of sensitive data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Account compromise, phishing, or further exploitation of the victim's session or data.

behavioral_signatures: User-generated content containing <script> tags or javascript: URLs in HTML attributes
Presence of overlay classes such as joyride-modal-bg in user content
Arbitrary data-* attributes or non-whitelisted classes in <figcaption> or widget HTML
Image tags with src or data-cke-saved-src attributes using the javascript: scheme
file_indicators: Content fields in the Drupal database containing <script> tags, javascript: URLs, or suspicious overlay class names
Unusual or non-whitelisted attributes in
Presence of data-cke-* attributes with unexpected values in stored content
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound HTTP or HTTPS requests triggered by user interaction with rendered content (e.g., redirection to external domains such as attacker.com)
JavaScript execution resulting in network requests to attacker-controlled domains or IP addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan user-generated content in the Drupal database and rendered pages for <script> tags, javascript: URLs in HTML attributes, and suspicious classes or data-* attributes in figcaption and widget HTML. Monitor for DOM elements with overlay classes or non-whitelisted attributes. Use web application firewalls (WAFs) to block known XSS payloads and monitor for suspicious outbound network activity originating from user interaction with content, such as redirections or JavaScript-initiated requests to external domains.
